target.title: fix: pin direct-provider Google signing key
target.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/issues/760.

## Summary

- Pin Google's Linux package-signing primary fingerprint in Go-generated direct-provider cloud-init.
- Import the downloaded key in an isolated temporary GnuPG home, export only the approved key, atomically install a source-scoped keyring, and bind the Chrome APT source with `signed-by`.
- Fail closed to the existing Chromium fallback when fingerprint verification fails.
- Replace the legacy global APT trust assertion with a regression contract and add an Unreleased changelog entry thanking @coygeek.

## Verification

- `go test ./internal/cli -run TestCloudInitBrowserWrapper -count=1`
- `go vet ./...`
- `go test -race ./internal/cli -run TestWindowsWSL2BootstrapCompleteProbeUsesWindowsMarker -count=3 -v` — three passes after one unrelated five-second timeout in the first repository-wide race run.
- `go test -race ./internal/cli -count=1` — passed in 119.896s.
- `go test -race ./...` — all provider and non-CLI packages passed; the first CLI package run had only the isolated WSL fake-SSH timeout above.
- `git diff --check`
- `/Users/steipete/Projects/agent-skills/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --parallel-tests 'go test -race ./internal/cli && go vet ./...' --stream-engine-output` — clean, no accepted/actionable findings; patch correct at 0.82 confidence.
